title: Course Knowledge Checks & Real Exam Questions
description: Interactive knowledge check questions extracted from official course materials and real ISA/IEC 62443 Cybersecurity Fundamentals exam banks.

questions.question: Which statement explains the purpose of the ISA/IEC 62443 series in securing Industrial Automation and Control Systems (IACS)?

options.text: To define a universal security framework that applies exclusively to IT networks
To provide general cybersecurity guidelines that do not require industry-specific customization
To establish a structured approach to cybersecurity tailored to industrial automation and control environments
To mandate specific technologies that all industries must use to secure IACS

questions.explanation: The ISA/IEC 62443 series is specifically designed to provide a flexible, structured framework tailored to industrial automation and control environments (IACS), accounting for operational safety, availability priorities, and ICS-specific architectures rather than generic IT networks or rigid technology mandates.

questions.question: What is the role of the ISA99 Committee in developing the ISA/IEC 62443 series?

options.text: Enforces cybersecurity laws for all industrial sectors
Focuses solely on IT security and does not address industrial automation
Creates security policies for government agencies rather than private industries
Develops and maintains the ISA/IEC 62443 standards to improve IACS cybersecurity

questions.explanation: The ISA99 Committee is the international consensus-based group responsible for developing, writing, and maintaining the ISA/IEC 62443 series of standards to enhance cybersecurity across industrial automation and control systems.

questions.question: What is the primary distinction between an Industrial Control System (ICS) and an Industrial Automation and Control System (IACS) as described in ISA/IEC 62443?

options.text: IACS refers only to cybersecurity controls, while ICS includes physical safety measures
ICS is a subset of IACS, focusing mainly on hardware and software, while IACS includes people, policies, and processes
ICS focuses solely on critical infrastructure, whereas IACS applies only to manufacturing environments
IACS is exclusive to North America, while ICS is a globally recognized term

questions.explanation: An Industrial Control System (ICS) typically denotes the physical hardware, software, and control equipment, whereas an Industrial Automation and Control System (IACS) encompasses the broader socio-technical ecosystem including people, operational policies, and organizational processes.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of ISA/IEC 62443-3-2 in IACS cybersecurity?

options.text: Focuses on cybersecurity risk assessment and system design, helping asset owners define security zones and conduits
Provides guidelines for cloud-based security in industrial environments
Mandates encryption standards for all industrial control networks
Describes hardware specifications required for industrial cybersecurity compliance

questions.explanation: ISA/IEC 62443-3-2 provides the standard methodology for assessing cybersecurity risk, conducting risk assessments, and designing secure industrial systems through the establishment of security zones and conduits.

questions.question: Why is the ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 standard critical for securing industrial control systems?

options.text: Specifies incident response plans for industrial cybersecurity breaches
Ensures full automation of cybersecurity processes in industrial environments
Establishes requirements for a secure product development lifecycle for control system components
Mandates immediate security patching for all industrial systems without exceptions

questions.explanation: ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 defines the mandatory requirements for a secure product development lifecycle (SDLC) that product suppliers must follow when designing, developing, and maintaining industrial control components.

questions.source: Real Exam Bank | ITExams / SecExams Q#1
questions.question: Which characteristic is MOST closely associated with the deployment of a demilitarised zone (DMZ) in industrial control networks?

options.text: Level 4 systems must use the DMZ to communicate with Level 3 and below.
Level 0 can only interact with Level 1 through the firewall.
Internet access through the firewall is allowed without restrictions.
Email is prevented, thereby mitigating the risk of phishing attempts.

questions.explanation: In Purdue reference model architectures, enterprise corporate IT systems (Level 4) communicate with plant operations (Level 3 and below) securely through an industrial DMZ.

questions.question: What are the connections between security zones called in the ISA/IEC 62443 framework?

options.text: Firewalls
Tunnels
Pathways
Conduits

questions.explanation: Conduits are defined as secure communication channels that connect two or more security zones and enforce traffic filtering and access control.

questions.question: How can defence in depth be achieved via security zones?

options.text: By having zones within zones, or subzones, that provide layered security
By having a zone edge that is using the security policies of the asset owner
By having zones that are connected via conduits using SSL encryption
By having zones that separate sensors from actuators to provide layered security

questions.explanation: Nesting security zones or creating subzones provides multiple concentric defensive layers, ensuring that an attacker breaching the outer plant zone still encounters internal security barriers.

questions.question: Whose responsibility is it to determine the level of risk an organisation is willing to tolerate?

options.text: Management
Legal Department
Operations Department
Safety Department

questions.explanation: Executive management holds ultimate responsibility for establishing corporate risk tolerance and governance policies under ISA/IEC 62443-2-1.

questions.question: What type of security level defines what a component or system is capable of meeting?

options.text: Capability security level (SL-C)
Achieved security level (SL-A)
Design security level
Target security level (SL-T)

questions.explanation: Security Level - Capability (SL-C) measures the built-in security features and capabilities that a product or system is designed to achieve.

questions.question: Which steps are included in the ISA/IEC 62443 assess phase?

options.text: Cybersecurity requirements specification and detailed cyber risk assessment
Cybersecurity requirements specification and allocation of IACS assets to zones and conduits
Detailed cyber risk assessment and cybersecurity maintenance, monitoring, and management of change
Allocation of IACS assets to zones and conduits, and detailed cyber risk assessment

questions.explanation: The assess phase under 62443-3-2 begins with partitioning the system into security zones and conduits followed by conducting a detailed cyber risk assessment.

questions.question: What is the standard formula for calculating risk in industrial cybersecurity frameworks?

options.text: Risk = Likelihood + Consequence
Risk = Threat - Vulnerability x Consequence
Risk = Threat + Vulnerability + Consequence
Risk = Threat x Vulnerability x Consequence

questions.explanation: Risk is fundamentally evaluated as a multiplicative function of Threat probability, Vulnerability susceptibility, and Consequence severity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically listed under Organizational Security Measures (SP Element 1 in 62443-2-1)?

options.text: Malware protection
Background checks
Supply chain security
Security awareness training

questions.explanation: Malware protection is a technical security countermeasure, whereas background checks, supply chain security, and awareness training are organizational policies.

questions.question: An organisation requires two different employees to approve any high-risk transaction. What is the name of this security principle?

options.text: Least Privilege
Separation of Duties
Job Rotation
Mandatory Vacation

questions.explanation: Separation of Duties prevents a single individual from having end-to-end control over critical tasks by dividing responsibility across multiple personnel.

questions.question: Which service does an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) provide in industrial network monitoring?

options.text: It acts as a physical lock on control room doors.
It is effective against all known and unknown network vulnerabilities.
It automatically blocks malicious activity in real time.
It detects attempts to break into or misuse a computer system.

questions.explanation: An IDS monitors network traffic and system events to detect unauthorized intrusion attempts or policy violations, alerting operators without actively blocking traffic (unlike an IPS).

questions.question: What is TRUE regarding industrial safety instrumented systems (SIS)?

options.text: No dedicated malware has ever been found targeting safety systems specifically.
Even the most modern and sophisticated safety systems can be defeated by a determined attacker.
Safety systems are completely independent protection layers and have zero cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
By integrating control and safety systems via Modbus TCP, cybersecurity risks are eliminated.

questions.explanation: Advanced industrial malware (such as Triton/Trisis) has demonstrated that safety systems can be targeted and compromised by sophisticated cyber attackers.

questions.question: What is considered one of the most important lines of defence in securing an industrial control system?

options.text: Knowledgeable and vigilant staff
Reducing the attack vector of Level 5 devices
Installing firewalls from a single preferred vendor
Implementing countermeasures defined exclusively in document 62443-3-3

questions.explanation: Technology alone cannot secure an industrial plant; well-trained, knowledgeable, and vigilant personnel are the ultimate line of defence against cyber attacks.
